content.definition: To prove P → Q, assume P and derive Q. Then close the assumption and conclude P → Q.
To prove P, assume ¬P and derive a contradiction. Then conclude P.

content.text: An assumption holds only inside its own part of the proof. Close it before you use the result.

examples.title: Indirect proof
lines: The premises are P ∨ Q and ¬Q. The goal is P.

question.prompt: How does a conditional proof prove P → Q?
question.hint: The assumption comes from the goal itself.
question.explanation: Assume the if part P, derive the then part Q, then close the assumption to conclude P → Q.
